title: Ten reviewed non-WebView test/tooling paths have stale generated navigation relationships
observed_behavior: Exact current-source joins found eight non-WebView PROJECT_INDEX source_hash values that do not match reviewed bytes and two additional tooling paths whose generated summaries are stale even though their PROJECT_INDEX rows are current. Source edits and partial generated refreshes therefore leave generated navigation and current semantic evidence describing different snapshots.
expected_invariant: Every generated navigation record used to route an audit review must bind to the same source hash as the review, or the stale relationship must remain explicit and finding-backed until the settled worktree is regenerated.
root_cause: Source edits and partial generated-summary refreshes occurred without an atomic refresh of PROJECT_INDEX, while concurrent changes continued after the audit baseline was captured.
failure_scenario: An agent navigates from PROJECT_INDEX or a stale summary and reviews obsolete symbols, dependencies, routes, or associated tests, then incorrectly claims complete current-hash coverage.
evidence: A structured final join over the 481 pending non-WebView W11 paths found 459 hash-matched PROJECT_INDEX records, 15 intentionally unindexed fixtures, and exactly seven stale records.

Current hashes for the three concurrently changed sources are test_application_facade_web_static.py 413d03f8..., test_application_facade_web_static_cross_page.py 0af0549d..., and test_metrics_feature.py a896f66b..., while PROJECT_INDEX still carries their immutable-baseline hashes.
Generated summaries are additionally stale for test_application_facade_local_api_http.py, test_application_facade_process_launch.py, and test_service_run_monitor.py.
AUDIT-FIND-COV-001 already establishes the repository-wide generated-context drift; this finding supplies the exact W11 path-local locations required by strict review reconciliation.

The current delta adds a stale PROJECT_INDEX join for tests/python/desktop/test_priority_queue_export.py: current SHA-256 c77b43f27dd1446d33ab77c4d54f14e43c8cd75c215bbd1d2298f24c414da6b5 versus indexed 1f1bbf4470cc67189b0614a5eff25b88f572963900fd8cc2bd9a0c284b4d6b78.

Generated summaries are stale for current check_test_suite_subsystem_inventory.py SHA-256 b7b5e20c18d07f3fd0daade80df3d5bac48dab12f74ec82606fb5288eb8f2f38 and test_test_suite_subsystem_inventory.py SHA-256 8e41784496153089b37a17f3ac96ecca5fd557c356753432ae3d7d4b4014e0d1, while their PROJECT_INDEX joins match.
existing_safeguards: Source hashes are present in PROJECT_INDEX and generated summaries; generator check modes and the audit ledger detect mismatches.
safeguard_gap: The artifacts are not refreshed as one frozen-worktree transaction, so consumers can observe a mixed generation and path-local terminal review requires an explicit finding.
tests_missing: A phase-boundary transaction that freezes writers and proves exact source-summary-index hash equality before review publication.
recommended_remediation: After concurrent writers quiesce, regenerate summaries and PROJECT_INDEX through canonical tooling, run all generated-context check modes, and rebind the central coverage matrix to the resulting current hashes.
remediation_risk: Low for deterministic regeneration; concurrent user changes must be preserved and the refresh must happen only after a writer freeze.
validation_rung: Generated-context check modes, exact source/summary/PROJECT_INDEX hash joins, and repository-audit current-content validation; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Path-local extension of the already confirmed repository-wide AUDIT-FIND-COV-001, without duplicating its root cause.

title: Release finalization overwrites pre-existing version history and cannot restore it on rollback
observed_behavior: _finalize refuses existing released packet targets but does not refuse or snapshot an existing metadata/history/<version> directory. It copies current metadata over same-named archived files and, on a later exception, leaves that pre-existing directory untouched rather than restoring its prior bytes.
expected_invariant: A versioned release-history directory must be immutable by default. Finalization must either refuse any existing version archive or transactionally preserve and restore every pre-existing archive byte on failure.
root_cause: The transaction snapshots live metadata and tracks only whether the archive directory existed; it neither preflights archive-file collisions nor snapshots archive contents before copy2 overwrites them.
failure_scenario: An operator finalizes a reused version label or retries after partial history creation. VERSION, manifest, changelog, or index history is overwritten; if summary publication or a later filesystem step fails, live metadata rolls back but the old release-history evidence remains irreversibly replaced.
evidence: Current finalize_release.py SHA-256 0d219425... checks only released packet targets at lines 217-220, copies archive files at 258-261, and calls _remove_created_dir with existed_before=True at 272.

An isolated temporary-directory probe pre-created history/1.0.0/VERSION with immutable-old-history and made RELEASE_SUMMARY.md a directory so the final write failed. The function raised PermissionError and restored live VERSION to old-live, but archived VERSION remained overwritten as 1.0.0.

Current test_change_control.py SHA-256 3a03979e... asserts rollback only when history/1.0.0 did not exist and expects the newly created directory to disappear; it has no pre-existing-history collision case.
Structured deduplication found no current finding located on this implementation or test path.
existing_safeguards: Released packet filenames are collision-checked, live metadata and packet sources are snapshotted, and newly created release/archive directories are removed during rollback.
safeguard_gap: Those safeguards do not cover a pre-existing archive directory, even though copy2 mutates it before the transaction is known to have succeeded.
tests_present: generator-failure rollback for a newly created archive directory
tests_missing: pre-existing archive byte preservation on failure
partial archive collision and retry cases
recommended_remediation: Fail before mutation when HISTORY_ROOT/<version> already exists unless a separately protected recovery mode is explicitly requested. If replacement is ever supported, snapshot the complete archive and publish via a new temporary directory plus atomic rename, with rollback proof.
remediation_risk: Medium: stricter immutability may change retry practices and requires a documented recovery path for partial releases.
validation_rung: Focused change-control tests covering new release, existing archive, partial archive, injected failures before and after archive publication, and exact byte-for-byte rollback; no real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from remote GitHub asset clobber and Git-observation failure: this finding concerns local version-history bytes overwritten inside the finalizer transaction.

title: Risky-file changed-path checks report success when Git enumeration fails
observed_behavior: changed_paths catches OSError and CalledProcessError and returns the same empty list as a genuinely clean diff. main then performs no classification and returns zero as long as the registry schema itself is valid; JSON output says ok true with no matches.
expected_invariant: A guard that selects validation obligations from changed paths must distinguish a successfully empty Git diff from an unavailable or failed Git query and fail closed when it cannot enumerate the change set.
root_cause: The Git helper collapses command failure into an empty collection, and the caller's exit status is based only on registry-definition findings rather than change-enumeration success.
failure_scenario: Git is missing, times out, encounters an invalid revision, or cannot read the repository while high-risk media, lifecycle, settings, or release files are changed. The canonical guard reports success and omits every required check and manual gate.
evidence: Current check_risky_file_registry.py SHA-256 f8df061b... returns [] on Git errors at lines 202-211 and returns 1 only for registry findings at line 272.
A read-only mock made subprocess.run raise CalledProcessError(128). main(['--changed','--json']) returned 0 with ok=true and matches=[].
Current test_risky_file_registry.py SHA-256 9209599f... has no changed_paths, Git-failure, or CLI exit-status test.
No current finding is located on either path; AUDIT-FIND-W11-013 has a related but distinct Git-failure-to-clean release-identity root.
existing_safeguards: Git subprocesses use check=True and registry schema validation still runs.
safeguard_gap: The check=True failure signal is immediately discarded, so the final success result attests only to registry syntax and can be mistaken for complete changed-path coverage.
tests_present: Registry schema and explicit-path classification tests
tests_missing: Missing Git executable, timeout, nonzero diff, invalid HEAD, and permission-failure cases
An invariant that an empty changed set is accepted only after a successful Git query
recommended_remediation: Return a structured enumeration result or propagate Git failures. Make --changed/--staged exit nonzero with actionable stderr when enumeration is unavailable, while retaining explicit --paths behavior for callers that already possess a trusted path set.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: Git-less callers will fail instead of silently passing and may need an explicit trusted --paths mode.
validation_rung: Focused unit and CLI tests for successful empty/nonempty diffs plus every Git failure class, followed by the canonical risky-file registry check.
prior_audit_relationship: New path-specific guard failure; related to but not duplicative of release identity falsely serializing failed Git status as clean.

title: Changed-summary refresh succeeds after Git diff enumeration fails
observed_behavior: git_changed catches CalledProcessError and returns an empty source list. Both the default incremental mode and explicit --changed mode treat that result as no work; explicit --changed calls cmd_generate([]), prints zero written/unchanged, and returns success.
expected_invariant: Incremental generated-context refresh must distinguish a verified empty diff from failed source enumeration and must not claim success when it cannot identify changed files.
root_cause: The Git helper erases failure state by using [] for both outcomes, and the generation path has no independent enumeration-success check.
failure_scenario: A post-edit summary refresh runs with invalid HEAD, Git permissions, or a failing diff command. It exits zero without refreshing changed summaries; stale navigation is then committed or used by the required summary-first workflow.
evidence: Current refresh_summaries.py SHA-256 1619894d... catches CalledProcessError at lines 677-680 and routes the empty list into successful generation at lines 805-814.
A read-only mock made subprocess.check_output raise CalledProcessError(128). main(['--changed']) returned 0 and printed 'Summaries: 0 written, 0 unchanged. Source files: 0.'
Current test_summary_integrity.py SHA-256 14dc2554... covers hash drift, orphans, roots, and generator behavior but contains no git_changed or Git-failure case.
Current W11 reconciliation found seven stale PROJECT_INDEX joins and three stale desktop summaries, showing why silent incremental no-ops matter even though this probe did not mutate generated files.
existing_safeguards: Full --check and --all modes can detect or repair drift, and summaries carry source hashes.
safeguard_gap: The prescribed incremental --changed command can falsely succeed before those broader checks run, and its output does not disclose a Git error.
tests_present: Summary hash, parser fingerprint, orphan, source-root, and generated-output integrity tests
tests_missing: Git diff nonzero, timeout, missing executable, invalid HEAD, and verified-empty-diff cases for default/--changed/--staged modes
recommended_remediation: Propagate or explicitly return Git enumeration failure and exit nonzero with stderr. Keep an empty list valid only when the Git command itself succeeds; add regression tests for all three incremental entry paths.
remediation_risk: Low: failing closed may expose unsupported Git-less usage, which should use --all or explicit --paths instead.
validation_rung: Focused summary-integrity tests with mocked Git outcomes plus canonical refresh_summaries --check and project-index check modes.
prior_audit_relationship: New incremental-refresh root cause; repository-wide generated drift was already recorded under AUDIT-FIND-COV-001.

title: Tdarr rebuild can recursively erase the entire shared TestLibraries root
observed_behavior: The containment check accepts equality with LocalBase/Scratch/TestLibraries, not only a child directory. If any caller-selected root contains a file with the sentinel name, rebuild invokes shutil.rmtree on that entire root without validating sentinel contents or root identity.
expected_invariant: A destructive fixture rebuild must target one tool-owned, uniquely identified child directory and must never accept the shared TestLibraries parent or authenticate ownership by filename alone.
root_cause: Path containment uses relative_to without rejecting the allowed-root equality case, while destructive authorization checks only sentinel existence and does not bind sentinel schema, generator identity, or canonical target path.
failure_scenario: A caller passes LocalBase/Scratch/TestLibraries as --library-root and that directory contains a stale, copied, or forged .tdarr-matrix-generator.json. --rebuild recursively deletes every unrelated test library below the shared parent.
evidence: Current materialize_tdarr_test_library.py SHA-256 1e62749c... accepts allowed-root equality at lines 234-239 and calls shutil.rmtree(library_root) at lines 244-251 after only sentinel.exists().

An isolated temporary-root probe created TestLibraries/UnrelatedSuite/manual-proof.txt plus a same-named sentinel at TestLibraries. prepare_library_root(TestLibraries, rebuild=True) accepted the parent, deleted the unrelated file, and recreated an empty TestLibraries directory.

Current test_materialize_tdarr_test_library.py SHA-256 b6fbdbaa... tests a path outside TestLibraries and a child lacking the sentinel, but not parent-root equality, a forged sentinel, or unrelated siblings.
AUDIT-FIND-W11-012 concerns the separate proof-pack rebuild accepting arbitrary sentinel-marked destinations; this finding covers the materializer's additional shared-parent deletion capability.
existing_safeguards: The target must resolve within TestLibraries, nonempty rebuild requires --rebuild, and a sentinel filename must exist.
safeguard_gap: The broad parent is itself considered within the boundary, and an unauthenticated filename cannot prove exclusive ownership of every descendant selected for recursive deletion.
recommended_remediation: Require library_root to be a strict descendant of TestLibraries and preferably equal a canonical tool-owned leaf or approved prefix. Parse and validate a sentinel containing canonical resolved root and generator identity before deletion; reject reparse-point ambiguity and add preservation tests.
remediation_risk: Medium: custom test-library destinations may need migration, and Windows reparse handling must remain correct.
validation_rung: Focused temporary-filesystem destructive-boundary tests for parent equality, forged sentinels, unrelated siblings, symlinks/reparse points, and the normal rebuild path; representative real media is neither required nor allowed.
prior_audit_relationship: Related sentinel-authentication pattern, but a distinct tool and uniquely broader target: the shared TestLibraries parent itself.

title: Malformed Tdarr evidence is silently omitted from path-containment audit
observed_behavior: iter_json_payloads catches JSONDecodeError for JSON and individual JSONL rows and yields nothing. audit_path_containment records no parse-integrity finding, so malformed evidence files or lines are omitted and the containment result can be empty.
expected_invariant: A proof audit must treat unreadable or malformed evidence as an explicit integrity failure; it must never equate unparseable evidence with evidence containing no escaped paths.
root_cause: The iterator was designed as a permissive best-effort extractor and discards JSON decoding failures without returning error state to the safety-sensitive containment caller.
failure_scenario: A crash, partial write, or tampering truncates evidence containing an output_path outside the Tdarr test root. The audit silently skips the file or line and reports no path_escaped_test_root or malformed-evidence finding, allowing incomplete proof to appear clean.
evidence: Current tdarr_matrix_audits.py SHA-256 137c934e... catches and continues/returns at lines 196-204, while audit_path_containment only iterates yielded payloads at lines 207-230.

An isolated probe first wrote valid escaped-path JSON and received path_escaped_test_root; after replacing the same file with truncated JSON, audit_path_containment returned [] and iter_json_payloads yielded [].

Current test_tdarr_matrix_audit.py SHA-256 455de22e... verifies every declared scan root with valid JSON but has no malformed JSON, partially malformed JSONL, unreadable file, or replacement-character case.
No matching current finding is located on the implementation or test path.
existing_safeguards: Valid parsed absolute path fields are checked against the library root and escapes produce critical findings.
safeguard_gap: The safeguard is bypassed before field traversal when parsing fails, and the caller has no count of skipped files or rows.
tests_present: Valid containment scans across every declared evidence root
tests_missing: encoding replacement and explicit skipped-record counts
recommended_remediation: Make evidence parsing return structured payload-or-error records. Emit at least an error finding for every malformed/unreadable file or JSONL line and make strict audit exit nonzero; preserve path and line diagnostics.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: historical malformed evidence will newly fail strict audit and may need explicit quarantine rather than silent acceptance.
validation_rung: Focused Tdarr audit unit tests with temporary malformed/unreadable evidence and strict exit-code assertions; no real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: New evidence-integrity root cause; prior Tdarr findings concern proof pruning and destructive destination authorization.

title: Progress-validation subtest loop exercises only its final invalid payload
observed_behavior: The test assigns four invalid progress payloads inside a subTest loop, but the assertRaises and model_validate call are dedented outside the loop. Validation therefore executes once against only the fourth payload; the first three subtests contain assignments but no assertion.
expected_invariant: Each invalid numerator/denominator shape named by a subtest must independently invoke validation and assert rejection so a regression in any one rule fails the suite.
root_cause: The assertRaises block was placed one indentation level outside both the for loop and subTest context.
failure_scenario: A later contract change starts accepting a determinate payload with a missing numerator, missing denominator, or numerator greater than denominator while still rejecting the final indeterminate-with-counts case. This test remains green despite its name and data table implying all four rules are protected.
evidence: Current test_run_monitor_contract.py SHA-256 cb804f2a... shows assignments at lines 481-488 and the sole validation call at lines 489-490 outside the loop.

A direct read-only probe invoked the current contract separately for all four values and confirmed all are presently rejected; the defect is missing regression coverage rather than a claim of current production acceptance.
AST/control-flow inspection confirms one model_validate call after the loop, not four calls within subtests.
No current finding is located on this test path.
existing_safeguards: The Pydantic contract currently rejects all four payloads, and other progress tests cover nonfinite values and OCR modes.
safeguard_gap: Current implementation correctness is not protected against three independent future regressions by this table-driven test.
tests_missing: Effective per-case calls for missing numerator, missing denominator, and numerator exceeding denominator
recommended_remediation: Move assertRaises and model_validate inside the subTest block, construct a fresh item per case to avoid mutation carryover, and optionally assert the relevant validation field/message.
remediation_risk: Low: test-only correction may reveal latent contract behavior changes.
validation_rung: Focused run-monitor contract module and a call-count/control-flow assertion or mutation test proving all four cases execute; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current test-control-flow gap; no matching finding was present in central or worker fragments.

title: Unreadable reference candidates are treated as deletion-ready in strict legacy checks

locations.symbol: legacy readiness collection and strict-failure tests

observed_behavior: _read_text catches every OSError and returns the same empty string as an empty readable file. reference_matches skips empty text, FamilyStatus.ready sees no files or references, and --strict returns zero because the read failure was erased before main's OSError handler.
expected_invariant: Strict deletion-readiness must fail closed when any candidate cannot be read; only a complete successful reference scan may declare a legacy family ready.
root_cause: The low-level text helper converts read errors to content, so the higher-level strict error handler never receives the exception and cannot distinguish incomplete evidence from an empty file.
failure_scenario: A tracked source or documentation candidate is locked, permission-denied, transiently unavailable, or otherwise unreadable while it still references a legacy surface. The strict report declares the family ready and can be used to authorize removal with an incomplete dependency scan.
evidence: Current check_legacy_removal_readiness.py SHA-256 9b57306e... returns '' on OSError at lines 290-294, skips empty content at lines 322-327, and returns success for ready strict statuses at line 466.

A read-only mock made Path.read_text raise PermissionError for a candidate. _read_text returned '', collect_family_statuses produced zero references and ready=True, and strict_failures returned an empty list.
Current test_legacy_removal_readiness.py SHA-256 694e1042... covers reference filtering, family file counts, shim classification, and ready/blocked lists but not any read failure.
No current finding is located on the implementation or test path.
existing_safeguards: main catches OSError from collection and exits 2, and strict mode fails when files or references are successfully observed.
safeguard_gap: _read_text swallows the exact exception the top-level safeguard expects, converting incomplete scanning into ready evidence.
tests_missing: Permission, sharing-violation, disappearance, decoding, and transient read-error cases
recommended_remediation: Propagate read errors or collect them as structured scan failures. Make strict mode exit nonzero whenever any candidate was unreadable, and include path/error diagnostics in text and JSON reports.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: strict checks may newly block in constrained environments and require operators to repair permissions before removal.
validation_rung: Focused legacy-readiness unit/CLI tests with injected read failures and successful empty files, then canonical strict checks for each family.
prior_audit_relationship: New fail-open scan-completeness root cause; no matching current finding was located.

title: Concurrency regression tests can hang indefinitely on the deadlocks they are meant to detect

locations.symbol: concurrent network lifecycle start thread joins

observed_behavior: Three regression tests start two to four default non-daemon threads and call thread.join() without a timeout or later alive assertion. If snapshot locking, registry-save synchronization, or network lifecycle serialization deadlocks, the test never reaches an assertion or emits a localized failure.
expected_invariant: Concurrency tests must own a bounded completion deadline and turn a deadlock into an actionable failure without leaving live workers that prevent the Python process from exiting.
root_cause: Happy-path thread coordination uses unbounded joins inside the test process instead of a terminable child-process harness or bounded joins with guaranteed worker release.
failure_scenario: A lock-order, condition-notification, or filesystem-serialization regression blocks one worker. The focused test and the canonical release unittest runner wait indefinitely until a coarse external job timeout kills the entire run, obscuring the responsible assertion and discarding other results.
evidence: Current test_application_facade_local_api_http.py SHA-256 84655d01... starts three threads at lines 388-390 and unconditionally joins them at 391-392.
Current test_network_inflight_registry.py SHA-256 fbfc6491... starts four threads at lines 38-40 and unconditionally joins them at 41-42.
ops/scripts/release/test_support.ps1 lines 215-220 and 238-256 directly await Python unittest discovery without an outer process timeout, amplifying a stuck join into a release-gate hang.
Both focused happy-path tests passed during this review; that proves current completion, not a bounded failure path.
Structured deduplication found only AUDIT-FIND-W11-WEB-001 for unbounded Node subprocesses; this thread/deadlock root is distinct.

Current test_application_facade_network_lifecycle.py SHA-256 afa1d38403f917b151c21b6b6c02ab01099eb590154bf29211df3f1e08ec93bf starts two threads at lines 732-734 and unconditionally joins them at lines 735-736.
existing_safeguards: Worker exceptions are collected in the registry test, and the snapshot test uses a later one-second polling deadline after joins return.
safeguard_gap: Neither safeguard executes while join is blocked; default non-daemon workers also keep the interpreter alive after a timed assertion unless the underlying wait is released.
tests_present: Happy-path concurrent snapshot and registry-save tests
tests_missing: Deliberate deadlock/stall cases proving bounded termination
A shared concurrency-test helper that detects and cleans up live workers
recommended_remediation: Prefer running deadlock-sensitive probes in a terminable child process with a conservative deadline. Otherwise use controlled daemon workers, bounded joins, explicit is_alive failures, and a guaranteed release/cancellation mechanism so failure cannot strand the interpreter.
remediation_risk: Medium: naive bounded joins can still leave live threads, so cleanup and Windows CI timing need explicit design.
validation_rung: Focused concurrency tests including synthetic stalled workers and canonical release-runner timeout behavior; no real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: New Python thread lifecycle root cause; related in impact but not duplicate of the existing Node subprocess timeout finding.

title: Marketecture test overwrites and deletes a fixed shared worktree file
observed_behavior: The pytest test accepts tmp_path but ignores it, writes a fixed repository path docs/generated/_marketecture_test_fixture.md, and unconditionally unlinks that path in finally.
expected_invariant: Tests must create fixtures only in isolated temporary roots and must never overwrite or delete a pre-existing developer or concurrent-run worktree file.
root_cause: The checker is exercised against the real repository root, so the test substitutes a globally named generated-doc path for the provided temporary fixture directory.
failure_scenario: A developer or concurrent task has a file at the fixed path. The test overwrites its bytes and deletes it even on a normal pass; if the process is interrupted before finally, it instead leaves test residue in the worktree.
evidence: Current test_marketecture_guard.py SHA-256 40cfb2fe... receives tmp_path at line 85 but writes REPO_ROOT/docs/generated/_marketecture_test_fixture.md at lines 86-87 and deletes it at line 92.
The fixed target was absent and untracked during the read-only review, so no destructive reproduction was performed against the shared worktree.
unittest discovery ran zero tests from this pytest-style module while pytest collect-only found 11; that separate discovery root is already AUDIT-FIND-W10-002.
No current finding is located on this test path.
existing_safeguards: A finally block removes the test file during ordinary completion, and the chosen filename is test-specific.
safeguard_gap: finally does not preserve prior contents and cannot run after abrupt process termination; a distinctive name is not exclusive ownership in a shared repository.
tests_present: The path-mode test verifies the guard returns failure for buzzword content
recommended_remediation: Build a minimal temporary repository under tmp_path, patch or inject the checker's repository root, write the fixture only there, and assert the real worktree is untouched. If a shared path is unavoidable, snapshot and restore prior bytes rather than unlinking blindly.
remediation_risk: Low: test-only isolation may require a small repository-root injection seam.
validation_rung: Focused pytest execution with a pre-existing sentinel file, parallel-run check, and post-test worktree cleanliness assertion; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from the existing unittest discovery omission: this finding concerns destructive fixture placement when pytest does execute the test.

title: Fresh audit-progress test fixture is deliberately future-dated beyond the stale-policy tolerance
observed_behavior: The test constructs audit progress with a naive local timestamp 60 seconds in the future and then expects the audit report bar to be active. The production status policy treats timestamps more than five seconds in the future as stale, so the isolated test deterministically receives status warning and fails at line 570.
expected_invariant: A positive fresh-progress test must use a timestamp that is fresh under the same clock and timezone contract as production, while future-clock-skew behavior is covered by a separate negative case.
root_cause: The fixture attempts to avoid expiration by adding 60 seconds, but future dating crosses the explicit five-second future-tolerance boundary and contradicts the behavior under test; its naive timestamp also depends on local timezone interpretation.
failure_scenario: The focused desktop snapshot suite or a release gate runs this case and fails even though production correctly marks implausibly future audit evidence as warning, obscuring unrelated regressions and preventing a clean deterministic validation result.
evidence: Current test SHA-256 2caf303bcbbc4448a386e357082a063460388175d5b49ea30d2b5beec6fecb15 sets last_update to datetime.now() + timedelta(seconds=60) at line 539 and expects active at line 570.
Current status_policy.py lines 186-194 marks any parsed timestamp more than five seconds ahead as stale; stale progress maps to warning.

The bundled-Python isolated unittest completed in 0.054 seconds and failed at line 570 with warning != active, so ordinary execution delay is not the cause; the failure is centrally recorded as AUDIT-ERR-COORD-170.
The prior exact-current review row incorrectly reported no findings for this path.
existing_safeguards: Production rejects materially future timestamps as stale and the test asserts the intended active status.
safeguard_gap: The assertion and fixture violate each other, leaving the intended positive contract untested and the focused suite red.
tests_present: Stale audit-progress warning case with a timestamp 30 minutes in the past
recommended_remediation: Use a timezone-aware current timestamp (or inject/freeze the clock) for the positive case. Add a separate fixture beyond the future-tolerance boundary and assert warning/stale behavior explicitly.
remediation_risk: Low: test-only clock control should align the case with existing production policy.
validation_rung: Run the focused snapshot unittest class under the bundled Python runtime, including fresh, stale-past, and future-skew boundary cases; no real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: Correction to the existing no-findings review row after the exact isolated test failed; no matching current finding was located.
